target_customer: Developers and device makers (IoT, apps, cars, TV) who want to add voice or text natural-language control
problem: Turning free-form speech or text from users into structured commands was hard for small teams to build; Siri-like capability had no developer API.
business_model: Developer API platform (free beta; planned usage-based), later free and open after the Facebook deal

founders.name: Alexandre Lebrun
founders.background_notes: Began coding Wit.ai with Blandin in April 2013 per a Medium profile.

founders.name: Laurent Landowski
founders.background_notes: YC page bio: cofounded VirtuOz and Wit.ai, later Nabla (healthcare). Role at Wit.ai not stated.

competitors.name: Ask Ziggy
competitors.what: Natural language understanding API without integrated processing engines

competitors.name: Nuance
competitors.what: Speech incumbent; offered a Siri-like integrable app/tools for developers, and had quietly bought the founder's earlier company VirtuOz

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed machine-learned language understanding across domains, a training workflow and speech integration; the founders had prior experience from VirtuOz.

defensibility.rationale: Pitched as an open community network: over 99% of developers agreed to share training data, a possible data moat; but language-understanding APIs were being copied (api.ai launched Sept 2014).

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch (Mar 2014) listed Amazon, Nuance and Intel as possible entrants; Facebook bought Wit.ai in Jan 2015 and kept the API open and free.

market_need_then: About 2,000 developer registrations within two months of beta, mostly word of mouth, and several signed customers (a device maker, a car company, a TV channel, home-automation startups) per TechCrunch, Mar 2014. Voice assistants like Siri had no developer API.

branding.domain_note: wit.ai domain used (TLD .ai); acquisition history of the domain not found.

brand_strength.rationale: Memorable short name and a clear positioning line used in YC and TechCrunch coverage; no mascot or brand-focused press found, so only moderate rating.

outcome_analysis: Wit.ai was started in spring 2013 (about April 2013) by a founder who had already sold a conversational-AI company, joined YC in W14, grew to thousands of developers by word of mouth, raised a $3M seed led by a16z in October 2014, and was bought by Facebook in January 2015, 21 months after founding. The exit came with an open, free platform and the team moving to Facebook; price undisclosed. Whether it was a product win or a talent-and-platform purchase is not stated in sources; later competitors (api.ai, bought by Google) show the space was contested.
notes: Acquisition price not disclosed; a French outlet's claim of $10M is unverified and not recorded. ZoomInfo lists NEA as lead (conflicts with TechCrunch/Medium; a16z used). PitchBook reportedly lists a ~$97K accelerator entry in 2014-03, not recorded. api.ai (Sept 2014) is after the batch and excluded from competitors. Web Archive unreachable.
